stem.text: A vertical shaft is drilled to an unknown depth D meters, where \( D > 2 \). The amount of dissolved salt per meter of depth is \( f(h) = 2 \sin{\left(\frac{h^{2}}{4} \right)} + 7 \) grams per meter for \( 0 \le h \le 2 \), where h is the depth in meters. Below depth 2 the amount per meter is an unknown continuous function g(h), and \( 0 \le g(h) \le b(h) \) for \( h \ge 2 \), where b is a function with \( \int_{2}^{\infty} b(h)\,dh = 12 \). Let T be the total amount of dissolved salt, in grams, along the whole shaft. Write an expression involving integrals for T, and explain why \( T \le 28 \). Use a calculator for any numerical work.

answer_key.label: \( T = \int_{0}^{2} f(h)\,dh + \int_{2}^{D} g(h)\,dh \), and \( T \le 28 \) because \( \int_{0}^{2} f(h)\,dh \approx 15.241 \) and \( \int_{2}^{D} g(h)\,dh \le \int_{2}^{\infty} b(h)\,dh = 12 \).

worked_solution.text: The model changes at depth 2, so split the total there: \( T = \int_{0}^{2} f(h)\,dh + \int_{2}^{D} g(h)\,dh \).
Since \( 0 \le g(h) \le b(h) \) and the interval from 2 to D lies inside the interval from 2 to infinity, \( \int_{2}^{D} g(h)\,dh \le 12 \). So \( T \le 15.241 + 12 < 28 \).

options.label: \( T = \int_{0}^{2} f(h)\,dh + \int_{2}^{D} g(h)\,dh + C \), and \( T \le 28 \) because \( \int_{0}^{2} f(h)\,dh \approx 15.241 \) and \( \int_{2}^{D} g(h)\,dh \le \int_{2}^{\infty} b(h)\,dh = 12 \).
options.derivation: a constant of integration attached to a sum of definite integrals

options.label: \( T = \int_{0}^{2} f(h)\,dh + g(D) - g(2) \), and \( T \le 28 \) because \( \int_{0}^{2} f(h)\,dh \approx 15.241 \) and \( \int_{2}^{D} g(h)\,dh \le \int_{2}^{\infty} b(h)\,dh = 12 \).
options.derivation: the integral of g from the split depth to D written as g(D) - g(split), as though g were its own antiderivative

options.label: \( T = \int_{0}^{2} f(h)\,dh + g(h), \text{ where } g(h) = \int_{2}^{D} g(h)\,dh \), and \( T \le 28 \) because \( \int_{0}^{2} f(h)\,dh \approx 15.241 \) and \( \int_{2}^{D} g(h)\,dh \le \int_{2}^{\infty} b(h)\,dh = 12 \).
options.derivation: the unknown function set equal to its own integral and substituted for the second piece
